business_patterns.top_pattern: Authorization code and facility mapping issues are masking true spend trends
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: CA, VA, GA, OH, PA / AUTH_CODE_DISTRIBUTION and Not Mapped facility classifications
key_driver_codes: Other Disorders of Nervous System with MCC
Kidney and Urinary Tract Infections without MCC
business_patterns.pattern_details: A large share of the observed increase is tied to authorization code distribution shifts and claims sitting in Not Mapped facility buckets. That means part of the signal may be administrative reclassification rather than true utilization or provider performance change. Business action on prior authorization policy, provider economics, or site-of-care should wait until these records are validated and reclassified.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: If this validation issue is not fixed first, downstream utilization, provider, and reimbursement actions may target the wrong problem.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Audit auth-to-claim mapping and facility crosswalks in CA, VA, GA, OH, and PA, reclassify Not Mapped claims, and then refresh the affected utilization and provider views before changing policy or contracts.
business_patterns.validation_reason: The increase is explicitly flagged as authorization or mapping movement, and several dollars sit in Not Mapped facility buckets that require data correction before business action.
evidence_summary: CA AUTH_CODE_DISTRIBUTION contributed +$2.2M, led by Other Disorders of Nervous System with MCC (+$0.7M) and Kidney and Urinary Tract Infections without MCC (+$0.6M).
VA AUTH_CODE_DISTRIBUTION added +$1.0M.
VA Not Mapped facility claims added +$375K on 25 more admissions, and GA Not Mapped added about +$180K across UTI and Ungroupable drivers.
OH / PA Not Mapped added +$101K in small-volume, high-paid cases.

business_patterns.top_pattern: CA acute hospital spend is concentrated in three PPO Local providers
key_driver_codes: Kidney and Urinary Tract Infections without MCC
Other Disorders of Nervous System with MCC
business_patterns.pattern_details: In CA PPO Local acute hospitals, spend is concentrated in three providers with two distinct drivers. UCI Medical Center and Huntington Health are mainly seeing more admissions, while Hoag Hospital Newport Beach shows both more admissions and higher paid per admit. This is a targeted provider-mix issue inside one product and facility setting, not a broad statewide pricing jump.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: Concentrated provider patterns can usually be addressed faster with targeted UM and network action than with broad policy changes.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Run provider-specific admission source and level-of-care review for UCI Medical Center and Huntington Health, and pair that with contract and reimbursement review for Hoag Hospital Newport Beach, focusing on recurring UTI and nervous system admissions.
evidence_summary: UCI Medical Center added +$0.6M with 27 more admissions, while paid per admit fell by about $0.4K.
Huntington Health added +$0.5M with 23 more admissions and largely flat paid per admit.
Hoag Hospital Newport Beach added +$0.7M with 24 more admissions and paid per admit up about $3.6K.
UTI and nervous system DRGs were recurring drivers, each adding about +$87K to +$140K.

business_patterns.top_pattern: CA complex IP Med/Surg admissions are driving a concentrated inpatient spike
key_driver_codes: Tracheostomy with Mechanical Ventilation >96 Hours or Principal Diagnosis Except Face, Mouth and Neck without Major O.R. Procedures
Infectious and Parasitic Diseases with O.R. Procedures with MCC
business_patterns.pattern_details: CA IP Med/Surg growth is being driven by a narrow set of complex sepsis, neurologic, respiratory failure, and UTI-related admissions rather than a broad inpatient trend. Some of the dollars reflect repeatable volume and intensity growth, while a meaningful share comes from very rare, very high-cost stays. This should be managed as a focused inpatient case-mix issue with both clinical and UM review.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: A small cluster of complex inpatient cases can move total spend quickly and may point to avoidable escalation, transfer, or severity-management gaps.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Launch targeted clinical case review on sepsis, neurologic, respiratory failure, and UTI admissions in CA IP Med/Surg, and pair it with UM review of admission appropriateness, ICU escalation, and transfer patterns at the named providers.
business_patterns.validation_reason: Several drivers are 1 to 2 admission outliers with very high paid per admit, so recurrence and coding accuracy should be confirmed before broader policy changes.
evidence_summary: CA IP Med/Surg new or rare high-cost cases added +$0.8M, including a tracheostomy/mechanical ventilation case at Huntington Health (+$131K) and sepsis with major O.R. procedures at UCI Medical Center (+$103K).
CA IP Med/Surg volume and intensity added +$0.8M, led by UTI site not specified (+$261K on 31 more admissions) and critical illness myopathy (+$160K).
Sepsis without prolonged ventilation added another +$95K at Hoag Hospital Newport Beach with 5 more admissions and paid per admit up about $1.6K.
Several rare drivers carried paid per admit from about $45K to $131K.

business_patterns.top_pattern: CA post-acute spend is rising across SNF, rehab, and NF
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: CA / PPO Local / SNF - FREE STANDING, Physical Rehab, NF
key_driver_codes: Other Disorders of Nervous System with MCC
business_patterns.pattern_details: CA post-acute spend rose across SNF - FREE STANDING, Physical Rehab, and NF. The pattern combines more post-acute volume with higher paid per admit in key SNF and rehab cells, plus a nursing-facility case mix weighted to neurologic, sepsis, cellulitis, and UTI cases. This points to a broader discharge and post-acute management opportunity rather than a single-provider issue.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: Post-acute use can extend total episode cost well beyond the acute admission and is often addressable through authorization, discharge planning, and steerage.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Review discharge disposition rules, SNF and rehab authorization criteria, and network steerage for neurologic, sepsis, cellulitis, and UTI cases in CA, with special focus on post-acute level-of-care selection.
evidence_summary: CA SNF - FREE STANDING added about +$0.6M across volume and mixed-cost groups, including 19 more admissions in one major driver and paid per admit up about $4.9K to $7.6K in key SNF cells.
CA Physical Rehab added +$211K on 5 more admissions with paid per admit up about $9.1K.
CA NF new or rare cases added +$257K, including anoxic brain damage and sepsis-related ungroupable stays.
CA NF volume and intensity added +$166K, including cellulitis of left lower limb (+$97K) and other toxic encephalopathy (+$70K).

business_patterns.top_pattern: OH and PA spend is concentrated in Lehigh Valley and Lee Memorial, with a high-cost inpatient tail
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: OH / PA / PPO Local / ACUTE HOSPITAL and SNF - FREE STANDING
key_driver_codes: Kidney and Urinary Tract Infections without MCC
Heart Failure and Shock with MCC
business_patterns.pattern_details: OH and PA spend is concentrated in Lehigh Valley Hospital - Cedar Crest and Lee Memorial Hospital, with more acute admissions and a smaller but meaningful tail of high-cost cardiac, respiratory, and sepsis cases. OH is more volume-led, while PA shows clearer paid-per-admit pressure at Lehigh Valley. This is best handled as a targeted provider and case-mix issue rather than a broad market-wide response.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: When a few providers account for most of the increase, targeted provider and care-management action offers the fastest path to impact.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Do provider-level review of admission drivers, case management, and reimbursement terms for Lehigh Valley Hospital - Cedar Crest and Lee Memorial Hospital, and add targeted clinical review of the rare high-cost IP Med/Surg cases.
evidence_summary: OH acute hospital PPO Local added +$0.5M, led by Lehigh Valley Hospital - Cedar Crest (+$211K) and Lee Memorial Hospital (+$117K) on 17 and 12 more admissions.
PA acute hospital spend at Lehigh Valley Hospital - Cedar Crest added +$305K with 10 more admissions and paid per admit up about $6.2K.
OH / PA rare IP Med/Surg cases added +$306K, including cardiac surgery for non-ST elevation myocardial infarct (+$95K) and heart failure or ventilator-supported respiratory failure cases.
PA SNF - FREE STANDING added +$69K with 9 more admissions.

business_patterns.top_pattern: VA costs are rising across the inpatient-to-SNF continuum
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: VA / PPO Local / ACUTE HOSPITAL and SNF - FREE STANDING
business_patterns.pattern_details: In VA, the same PPO Local population shows higher spend in both acute hospitals and SNF - FREE STANDING. Acute growth is mostly more admissions, while SNF adds both more admissions and higher paid per admit, pointing to rising costs across the inpatient-to-post-acute continuum. This suggests the management opportunity sits across discharge planning and post-acute utilization, not just inpatient authorization.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: Managing only the acute stay would miss a meaningful share of the follow-on cost.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Trace inpatient discharges to SNF in VA and tighten concurrent review, discharge planning, and SNF authorization criteria for this PPO Local population.
evidence_summary: VA acute hospital PPO Local added +$0.7M with 46 more admissions and essentially flat paid per admit.
VA SNF - FREE STANDING added +$0.4M with 37 more admissions and paid per admit up about $1.2K.
Both increases sit in auth-required services, indicating broader utilization pressure across the care continuum.

business_patterns.top_pattern: GA shows a recurring cellulitis and UTI pathway problem across acute and post-acute care
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: GA / PPO Local / ACUTE HOSPITAL, Physical Rehab, IP Med/Surg, NF
key_driver_codes: Kidney and Urinary Tract Infections without MCC
business_patterns.pattern_details: GA shows a coherent cellulitis and UTI story across acute hospital, Physical Rehab, IP Med/Surg, and NF. The largest dollars come from acute hospital admissions, but the same diagnoses recur in clinical case-mix groups, suggesting avoidable admission and post-acute pathway opportunities rather than isolated noise. This pattern should be worked through diagnosis-specific clinical and UM action.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: Repeated diagnosis clusters across settings often signal a manageable care-pathway problem with both inpatient and post-acute cost consequences.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Launch a joint clinical and UM review for cellulitis and UTI admissions in GA, including observation versus inpatient use, IV antibiotic pathways, and rehab transition criteria.
evidence_summary: GA acute hospital PPO Local added +$0.4M, led by Cellulitis without MCC (+$213K on 28 more admissions) and Kidney and Urinary Tract Infections without MCC (+$206K on 25 more admissions).
GA IP Med/Surg cellulitis cases added +$241K, including left lower limb (+$125K) and right lower limb (+$90K), with paid per admit up about $2.3K.
GA Physical Rehab added +$150K on 7 more admissions.
GA NF cellulitis cases added about +$78K across left lower limb and face.

business_patterns.top_pattern: Small-market and low-volume outliers need case-by-case triage, not broad policy action
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: CA / PA, CT / IN / NY, IN / ME / OH, ME, NY / small-volume acute, SNF, critical access, and rare IP Med/Surg outliers
key_driver_codes: Craniotomy with Major Device Implant or Acute Complex CNS Principal Diagnosis with MCC or Chemotherapy Implant or Epilepsy with Neurostimulator
business_patterns.pattern_details: Several smaller segments show emerging outliers, but each is based on low volume and should be handled as a targeted exception. The mix includes small-market SNF pressure, isolated acute hospital spikes, a ME critical access increase, and two one-case craniotomy stroke admissions in CA / PA. These are important to triage, but they do not yet support broad utilization, reimbursement, or network changes.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: Low-volume outliers can distort trend views and lead to overreaction if treated as durable patterns.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Route these cases for case-by-case validation and clinical review, confirm recurrence, and only escalate to policy or network action if the pattern repeats.
business_patterns.validation_reason: Most included groups are explicitly low-baseline or small-n outliers, including several 1 to 2 admission events.
evidence_summary: Small-market SNF pressure added +$159K across IN / ME / OH, with paid per admit up about $2.5K to $5.6K.
CT / IN / NY acute hospital outliers added +$149K, including a 1-admission ungroupable CT case of +$55K.
ME CRITICAL ACCESS added +$44K from 2 admissions with paid per admit about $21.8K higher.
CA / PA craniotomy stroke cases added +$119K across 2 one-admission cases at UCI Medical Center and Lehigh Valley Hospital - Cedar Crest.

executive_summary.headline: The main story is a mix of gating authorization and mapping issues, concentrated CA provider and post-acute pressure, and several state-specific inpatient and post-acute spikes that require targeted action rather than broad policy moves.
executive_summary.primary_business_message: First, a meaningful share of the observed increase is administrative: AUTH_CODE_DISTRIBUTION shifts and Not Mapped facility buckets must be corrected before acting on utilization or provider results. After that cleanup, the biggest actionable patterns are concentrated CA PPO Local acute-hospital and post-acute pressure, plus state-specific provider and diagnosis clusters in VA, OH / PA, and GA. Smaller multi-state outliers should be triaged individually because they are low volume and not yet durable patterns.
recommended_focus_order: Resolve AUTH_CODE_DISTRIBUTION and Not Mapped classification issues before changing PA, provider, or reimbursement strategy.
Address CA PPO Local concentration in ACUTE HOSPITAL, IP Med/Surg, and post-acute settings through coordinated UM, clinical, and network action.
Target VA, OH / PA, and GA with provider-specific and diagnosis-specific interventions rather than broad market-wide changes.

notes: All 37 analytical groups were assigned into 8 business patterns.
Coding validation and Not Mapped facility groups were intentionally consolidated into one gating validation pattern.
Low-volume multi-segment outliers were consolidated into one emergence pattern to preserve coverage without overstating immature trends.
Segment attribution is weak for 54% of cards (47 of 87) on segment_by [service_area_state]; add those dimensions to the stage's dimension or carry-through list to attribute them at cell level.
Merged 12 immaterial segment group(s) into residual groups labelled with their literal segment values.
